subject: Audit & access logs: delivery windows, residency guarantees, and secure erase
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@ghx.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Reynolds <paul.reynolds@ghx.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Audit & access logs: delivery windows, residency guarantees, and secure erase

Hi Vivek / Aditya —

We're working through procurement and the security review at GHX. Two asks from our InfoSec and procurement teams:

1) For audit logs and access logs generated by hosted tenants in EU regions, what are the configurable retention windows by plan (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)? We need concrete maximum and default values for both log types.

2) We need to know export capabilities — can we request on-demand bulk exports of a specific time range (for example: full audit logs for 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31)? If so:
   - Supported export formats (JSON / CSV / Parquet?)
   - Delivery mechanisms (S3 push, pre-signed URL, SCP) and whether exported artifacts can be delivered to our EU S3 with customer KMS keys.

3) Deletion guarantees — after a retention window elapses or after we request a tenant purge, how long until data is irrecoverably removed? Are there soft-delete windows or backups that extend that timeline?

We're under a short procurement deadline; can you outline the operational steps and expected lead times for a bulk export and for a formal confirmation on deletion/residency? I'll attach our vendor security questionnaire.

Thanks —
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Senior InfoSec Manager, GHX

Attachment: GHX_vendor_questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@ghx.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Paul Reynolds <paul.reynolds@ghx.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit & access logs: delivery windows, residency guarantees, and secure erase

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then we'll get Mina and Aditya to add implementation detail and timings.

- Retention defaults / caps (hosted EU tenants):
  • Access logs (API requests, token usage): default 90 days on Hosted plan; can extend to 365 days on Enterprise/Reserved (Dedicated) with an add-on; Private deployments: fully configurable by customer up to multi-year depending on storage commit.
  • Audit logs (admin actions, config changes): default 365 days on Enterprise; Hosted defaults to 180 days for standard accounts. Dedicated/Private can be set to customer requirements.

- Exportability:
  • We support on-demand bulk exports for both access and audit logs. Time-range exports (arbitrary start/end) are supported back to retention window limits — we cannot export beyond the retention window after data has been irreversibly purged.
  • Formats: JSON (newline-delimited), CSV, and Parquet (columnar) are supported.
  • Delivery: S3 push (preferred), pre-signed S3 URLs for customer pull, and secure SCP/HTTPS transfer. For EU residency we can deliver to your EU S3 bucket. For Dedicated/Private we support customer KMS/HSM — for Hosted we can push to your S3 using an upload role; we also support customer-side KMS encryption for objects we write (requires an integration step).

- Deletion / irrecoverability:
  • Soft-delete: when you request a tenant purge we mark log objects for deletion and retain them for a 30-day safety window by default to allow recovery and legal holds.
  • Hard-delete: after the safety/soft-delete window expires, objects are shredded and removed from primary storage; however, backups and snapshots are on a separate lifecycle and are pruned according to retention — typical maximum lag for purged items to be removed from backups is 60 additional days in Hosted. Dedicated/Private deployments can have the backup retention adjusted to meet contractual guarantees.

I'll loop Mina for the exact export SLA, encryption flow, and what we can commit to contractually for GHX. Attached a quick export spec (log_export_spec_v1.xlsx) that shows formats and sample file sizes.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachment: log_export_spec_v1.xlsx (XLSX, table of formats & estimated sizes)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@ghx.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Paul Reynolds <paul.reynolds@ghx.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit & access logs: delivery windows, residency guarantees, and secure erase

Hi Samantha —

Following up with the security/operations specifics you asked for. I've broken this down into concrete commitments vs typical behaviour: 

1) Retention by log type (concrete):
   - Hosted (standard): Access logs 90 days (default), Audit logs 180 days (default).
   - Enterprise/Dedicated: Access logs up to 365 days, Audit logs up to 3 years — configurable per contract.
   - Private/on-prem: fully customer-controlled.

2) Export mechanics & security:
   - Supported export formats: newline-delimited JSON (preferred for events), CSV, Parquet. Files include an export manifest (MD5/SHA256 checksums) and a redaction map if fields are redacted.
   - Delivery options: 
       * Push to customer S3 (we assume an upload role you provide) — supports server-side encryption with your KMS (we store the object encrypted at rest in your target bucket).
       * Pre-signed S3 URLs for pull (short-lived).
       * SFTP/SCP to customer-managed endpoint (mutual-TLS option).
   - Exports are logged and auditable: the export job creates an immutable Export Audit Record (who requested, timeframe, files produced, checksums). That record is retained alongside the tenant audit logs for the configured retention window.

3) Deletion guarantees (differentiated):
   - Tenant purge request: we perform an immediate logical purge and trigger the soft-delete retention (default 30 days) to prevent accidental loss. Customers may elect to waive the soft-delete to accelerate hard deletion.
   - Backups & snapshots: Hosted backups are retained for up to 60 days beyond primary retention; we can narrow that in contract for Dedicated/Private.
   - Irreversible deletion (certificate): for Dedicated/Private we can provide an erase certificate showing object manifest removal and snapshot destruction dates; Hosted customers receive a standard deletion attestation (scope limited by multi-tenant backup windows).

4) Additional notes on residency & cross-region copies:
   - We do not replicate EU tenant logs to non-EU regions by default. Cross-region replication only occurs if expressly configured (for DR) and must be part of the tenancy configuration.
   - For contract language requiring EU-only residency, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment to avoid multi-tenant backup holdings crossing boundaries.

If you want a formal statement for procurement I can draft a short deletion & export guarantee paragraph for inclusion in your SOW.

—Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
Attachment: audit_export_schema.json (JSON, contains field list & examples)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@ghx.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Paul Reynolds <paul.reynolds@ghx.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit & access logs: delivery windows, residency guarantees, and secure erase

Hi Samantha —

Operational steps & estimated timelines for an on-demand export (example: full audit logs for calendar year 2025):

1) Request: GHX opens a ticket to support@redwood.ai with the tenant ID, time range, desired format, and delivery method. Include the S3 bucket ARN and upload role if you want S3 push.

2) Validation (1 business day): we validate access, residency constraints, and whether data still exists in primary storage/backups. We return an estimated size and cost if beyond your included allocation.

3) Scheduling & Preparation (1-3 business days): for exports < 1TB we typically schedule within 2 business days; for larger datasets we coordinate a bulk window. We produce an Export Job record and manifest.

4) Delivery (1 day typical for S3 push once export completes): we push and provide checksums and a signed delivery manifest.

5) Post-delivery & erase: once you confirm receipt and signature of manifest, we can start the customer-requested purge path immediately (soft-delete window applies unless waived).

SLA examples: standard hosted export under 1TB = target 5 business days end-to-end; Enterprise customers can contract faster SLAs. Costs: minimal for small exports, incremental for multi-TB (we'll quote).

I also uploaded a concise playbook to our shared drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/ghx-export-playbook — it contains sample CLI steps for creating the S3 upload role, example export jobs, and a template mutual-action plan.

If you want, I can convert this into a single-page statement that procurement can accept (retention numbers + deletion wording).

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(Inline snippet)
Export CLI example:
redwoodctl export create --tenant ghx-prod --from 2025-01-01 --to 2025-12-31 --format ndjson --deliver s3://ghx-logs-eu/exports/2025 --role-arn arn:aws:iam::GHX_ACC:role/redwood-upload

Estimated size: ~240GB (ndjson), will split into 64MB gzipped parts for efficiency.

Vivek / Mina / Aditya —

This is very helpful, thank you. Procurement wants a short paragraph to insert into the SOW that confirms:
  - default and maximum retention for audit vs access logs for Hosted EU tenants,
  - that GHX can request an on-demand bulk export in NDJSON/Parquet and receive via S3 with customer KMS,
  - the customer-requested purge process (soft-delete 30 days, ability to waive soft-delete, and Hosted backup window up to 60 days).

Can you please draft that paragraph and send back today? Also please confirm the export SLA example you mentioned (Hosted export <1TB = 5 business days).

I'll attach the completed vendor questionnaire and open the support ticket once we have the SOW language.

Thanks again —
Samantha
